references.text: God calls Bezalel and Oholiab by name and fills them with wisdom and spirit to carry out the work on the tabernacle. This is the original appointment that Exodus 36:2 refers back to.
Moses announces to the people that the Lord has called Bezalel and Oholiab and given them wisdom to perform all kinds of artistic work. This is the immediate context before Exodus 36:2.
Describes how everyone whose heart was willing brought gifts for the Lord's work. The expression 'נְשָׂאוֹ לִבּוֹ' (his heart moved him) is used in a similar way.
God gives wisdom in the heart to craftsmen to make Aaron's priestly garments. The same concept of God-given wisdom in the heart ('חָכְמָה בְּלִבּוֹ').
Solomon asks for an understanding heart so that he may judge the people. The theme of God-given wisdom in the heart is central.
The Lord gives wisdom, and from his mouth come knowledge and understanding. Wisdom comes from God, just as it was given to the craftsmen.
An encouragement to ask God for wisdom, which he gives to all. The theme that wisdom is a gift from God.
Paul describes various spiritual gifts given by the Holy Spirit for service in the church. A parallel to how God equips people with different abilities for his service.
Complementary accounts of the same event: the people first give materials (35:29), then they carry out the work with wisdom (36:2).
The beginning (the call to the work) and the end (confirmation of completed obedience) in the building of the tabernacle.
Direct prophetic precursor and fulfillment: God's promise of wisdom (31:6) becomes reality when they are called to the work (36:2).
